summary: THREE target rows, THREE stored types CONFIRMED, and zero type_corrections — AFL is right on all three and animefillerguide is the source that lied, in two different ways. Premise re-read on the live AFG page first: row 32 is red-classed '* Filler' with chapters 'N/A'; row 38 is red-classed '* Filler' with 'N/A'; row 36 is BLUE with chapters '36, 37' and the note 'In this episode, there are changes compared to the manga. During the fight between Maka, Black Star, and Kid against Mosquito, Maka attacks and splits him in half. This does not happen in the manga: Maka never attacks, and instead Mosquito undergoes a more powerful transformation, forcing the three students to flee. (You can verify this in chapter 37 of the manga, from page 18 onward.)' — so on row 36 AFG makes NO filler claim at all: it maps two mainline chapters positively and its note is a FAITHFULNESS observation. The 'canon/mixed' contradiction on 36 is an artifact of reading AFG's blue CLASS as a type; the wave-1 lesson holds (the note is evidence, the class is an opinion). EP 32 'Legend of the Holy Sword 3' — CANON, position-less (A44). The episode adapts Atsushi Ohkubo's own BONUS chapter, 'Legend of the Holy Sword' (聖剣伝説), printed at the back of tankobon volume 9 between ch 32 and ch 33. souleater.fandom's Episode 32 page states it in its lead ('It is adapted from the bonus chapter "Legend of the Holy Sword"') and its Chapter 32.5 page states the reverse ('a bonus chapter of the manga Soul Eater. It was reprinted in tankobon form in Volume 9 ... adapted [as] Episode 32', page number = 31, anime correspondent = Episode 32). en-Wikipedia's List of Soul Eater chapters prints volume 9's contents INDEPENDENTLY as '032. The Corner of the Room / Bonus. "The Legend of the Holy Sword" (聖剣伝説) / 033. Retaliation Class / 034 / 035' — the extra is real, it is printed inside the source, and it carries NO mainline number (the fandom's '32.5' is a wiki convention, not a printed number). ja-Wikipedia independently calls eps 17 and 32 '聖剣伝説回'. So AFG's 'N/A' chapter cell is honest about the NUMBER and its red class is the error: AFG conflated 'no numbered chapter' with 'filler'. Under the GTO precedent (a side story serialized inside the source IS the source) the row is canon; under A44 it can never carry an anchor, exactly like bleach ep 46's side_story{-17}. Nothing is stranded: ep 31 ends at ch 32 and ep 33 starts at ch 33, so the anchor gap at 32 is correct as it stands. EP 36 — CANON, stored anchor (END 37, START 36, {36-37, ch 37 only through ~p.30}) CONFIRMED unchanged. souleater.fandom's Episode 36 lead: 'Its corresponding chapter from the manga is Chapter 37'; its Chapter 37 page: 'It was adapted as Episode 36'. en-WP's episode summary walks the same beats as the fandom's Chapter 37 summary (Giriko vs Justin, the seven-way Resonance Link, Shadow Star, Death Cannon, the new Genie Hunter, BREW lost to Arachnophobia, Eruka delivering the REAL Brew to Medusa, the snake in Marie). The fandom's own 'Manga and Anime Differences' list is six ALTERATIONS OF THE SOURCE'S OWN EVENTS (Majin Hunt used here rather than in ch 42; Mosquito seemingly destroyed rather than escaping via his 200-years-ago form; Kilik's human-shield gag; Black Star's internal line spoken aloud; Spirit's gag; Medusa's tense) — the T28 FAITHFULNESS clause, `divergence`, never a weight toward mixed. AFG's own note is the same observation, keyed to ch 37 p.18 onward. EP 38 'Asura's Temptation' — CANON, stored anchor (END 39, START 38) CONFIRMED. The fandom's Episode 38 infobox carries 'anime correspondent = Chapter 38 and Chapter 39' and its lead names ch 39; the reverse index holds on both chapter pages (Chapter 38: 'the argument between Black Star and Death the Kid, as well as Joe Buttataki's arrival to Death City, were adapted as part of Episode 38'; Chapter 39: 'The fight between Black Star and Death the Kid was adapted as Episode 38'). The SECOND source is en-Wikipedia's List of Soul Eater episodes, whose lead reads 'After episode 38, the anime deviated from the manga it was based on which lead to an anime original ending not found in the source material' — 38 is the last manga-based row, exactly the stored batch-19 ruling. The episode's spine is ch 38-39 (Joe's arrival and the Death Room meeting; Naigus's Uncanny-Sword ban relayed by Tsubaki; Black Star's balcony rumination; the spire smash and the Black Star vs Kid duel; the madness-wavelength reveal and Kid ending the fight; Medusa's decision to dispose of Crona) with heavy recasting (Joe arrives as a tech engineer, not an internal investigator; ch 39's fatal outcome is never adapted) plus short studio tags. That is `divergence` under the faithfulness clause, not an original story. ja-Wikipedia's blanket prose ('第36話までは原作の展開を踏襲していたが … 第37話以降はアニメオリジナルストーリー') is the one dissent and it is a BLOCK statement, not a per-row claim — it is already accounted for by the stored rulings (37 filler, 39-51 filler) and it is contradicted per-row by both chapter pages' reverse index and by en-WP's 'after episode 38'. No type_corrections, no anchor changes, one new side_story fact and two enriched divergence facts.

anchor_hostile.why: A44 position-less, NOT A1 — the row is CANON (stored type and AFL confirmed), but its source is an UNNUMBERED bonus chapter and there is no chapter number it could hold. Ohkubo's 「聖剣伝説」 ('Legend of the Holy Sword') is printed at the back of tankobon volume 9, between ch 32 and ch 33; en-Wikipedia's volume-9 contents list it as 'Bonus.' with no number, and souleater.fandom's '32.5' is that wiki's own convention (its Chapter 32.5 page: 'a bonus chapter ... reprinted in tankobon form in Volume 9', 31 pages, anime correspondent = Episode 32). Anchoring it would have to invent a number in the mainline space. The mainline line is intact without it: ep 31 -> END 32 (stored, {30-32}) and ep 33 -> 33 (stored), so no mainline chapter is stranded by leaving ep 32 position-less. The vol-9 volume field is a fact, not a position: the bonus sits in v9 (our boundary table v9 = 32-35). This is the bleach ep-46 shape (side_story{-17} + A44), delivered as a side_story annotation instead of a number.

annotations.chapters: the unnumbered bonus chapter 「聖剣伝説」 'Legend of the Holy Sword' (31 pages), printed at the back of tankobon volume 9 between ch 32 and ch 33
annotations.note: weight: SIGNIFICANT — because the bonus chapter IS the episode's plot end to end, not a fragment of it: Hero reading Excalibur's book in the library, the errand-boy humiliations, the trip to the Eternal Cave, the 1000 Provisions, the DWMA students' failed challenge, and the break-up over Excalibur's sneezing. souleater.fandom's Episode 32 lead states the derivation ('It is adapted from the bonus chapter "Legend of the Holy Sword"'), its Chapter 32.5 page states the reverse ('anime correspondent = Episode 32'), and en-Wikipedia's List of Soul Eater chapters prints volume 9's contents independently as '032. The Corner of the Room / Bonus. "The Legend of the Holy Sword" (聖剣伝説) / 033. Retaliation Class' — an UNNUMBERED extra printed INSIDE the source, so the mainline anchors are unaffected (N35: an unnumbered extra is a FACT, never a number; A44: no position). Material is NEW — its sole adaptation (the chapter page lists Episode 32 only). Do not confuse it with the anime's other two Excalibur episodes: ep 9 「聖剣伝説」 adapts mainline ch 6 「聖剣」 (stored anchor) and ep 17 「聖剣伝説2」 is anime-original (AFL and AFG agree: Filler / N/A) — ja-Wikipedia groups 17 and 32 together only as '聖剣伝説回', by subject, not by source.

annotations.chapters: the vol-9 bonus chapter 「聖剣伝説」
annotations.note: The non-source share is EXPANSION of the bonus chapter's own material, not a second plot, so the row stays canon under the T28 faithfulness clause. souleater.fandom's 'Manga and Anime Differences' section itemises it: the episode shows many of Excalibur's provisions the manga never depicts; Ox Ford's jealous rage over Hero is added; the fairies' life in the Eternal Cavern (flowers blooming in Excalibur's absence, the beer party) is added; Maka and Soul are expanded from a one-panel cameo into recurring witnesses; Sid's conversation about Hero is moved from female students to Lord Death over tea; and the manga's Hero-gropes-Kim beat is cut. Every one of these sits inside the chapter's own story (Hero fulfilling the 1000 Provisions), which is why the row is canon rather than mixed.

ENRICHMENT of the stored divergence{37} fact with animefillerguide's page-level note, read directly off the live page: 'During the fight between Maka, Black Star, and Kid against Mosquito, Maka attacks and splits him in half. This does not happen in the manga: Maka never attacks, and instead Mosquito undergoes a more powerful transformation, forcing the three students to flee. (You can verify this in chapter 37 of the manga, from page 18 onward.)' souleater.fandom's own 'Manga and Anime Differences' section states the same two facts from the other side — Maka unleashes Genie Hunter / Majin Hunt here, whereas in ch 37 Soul stops the battle on the 20-minute magnetic-field deadline and Maka does not first use Majin Hunt until ch 42; and Mosquito is seemingly destroyed here, whereas in ch 37 he escapes by threatening his form from 200 years ago. weight: these are ALTERATIONS OF THE SOURCE'S OWN EVENTS, which under T28's faithfulness clause keep the row CANON — they are not an original story share and carry no weight toward mixed. The stored fact (ep 36 stops one scene short of the end of ch 37, ~p.30, substituting an anime-original outcome for the chapter's closing Death Room / Internal Investigation scene) stands alongside this and is not contradicted: the two describe different parts of the same chapter (the fight outcome from p.18, the missing closing scene after ~p.30).

ENRICHMENT of the stored divergence{38-39} fact with the per-segment accounting the ask requires. SOURCE segments, weight SIGNIFICANT because together they are the episode's spine and its centrepiece: (a) Joe Buttataki's arrival at the DWMA and the Death Room meeting with Lord Death — ch 38's opening, recast (in the manga Joe arrives as an internal investigator hunting a mole; here he arrives to build weapons from demon tools); (b) Naigus's ban on the Uncanny/Enchanted Sword mode relayed to Black Star through Tsubaki — ch 38; (c) Black Star's balcony rumination on his losses to Mifune and Mosquito and the Will of the Nakatsukasa — ch 38; (d) Medusa and Eruka concluding that Crona's loyalty is unstable and that Crona may have to be disposed of — ch 38-39; (e) the spire smash, the challenge, and the full Black Star vs Death the Kid duel refereed by Sid and Naigus, ending in the madness-wavelength reveal (Black Star's wavelength matches his father White Star) and Kid putting him down — ch 39, and by far the longest sequence in the episode. ORIGINAL segments, weight NOT story-carrying: Kid's underground confrontation with Joe and Joe reaching the Secret Vault; the Uncle Bob's Rumba Coffee running gag and its closing punchline; Arachne and Mosquito on the Moral Manipulation Machine built from Eibon's blueprints; Stein collapsing in the Patchwork Laboratory; Crona in the DWMA dungeon; the infirmary tag and the Tsubaki/Kid spire tag (the fandom notes neither happens in the manga). Also NOT adapted: ch 39's climax, Joe Buttataki's murder, and Maka's discovery of Medusa's survival and Crona's treachery (the fandom: 'Her discovery would not happen until a later episode') — those are the stored 'ch 39's fatal outcome is never adapted' fact, unchanged.

structure.notes: STORED TYPES CONFIRMED ON ALL THREE ROWS — no type_corrections, deliberately. Row identity FIRST (R20, no index joins): AFL's soul-eater page holds 51 data rows, AFG's holds 51, ours holds 51, and rows 30-40 were matched on TITLE and (for AFL) DATE — AFL 32 'Legend of the Holy Sword 3 - The Academy Gang Leader's Tale?' 2008-11-10, 36 'Unleash the Seven's Resonance Link!' 2008-12-08, 38 'Asura's Temptation - The Big Man's Uncontainable Irritation?' 2008-12-22, all three exactly our stored titles and dates. AFL types all three 'Manga Canon' and turns to 'Anime Canon' only at 39. AFG's arc headers differ from ours but its numbering does not. WHICH SOURCE LIED, and how: animefillerguide, twice and differently. (1) On rows 32 and 38 it prints a red '* Filler' class with a chapter cell of 'N/A'. On 32 the 'N/A' is HONEST about the chapter NUMBER — the source is an unnumbered tankobon bonus chapter that AFG's chapter column cannot express — and the red class is the error: it conflates 'no numbered chapter' with 'no source'. On 38 both cells are simply wrong: two chapter pages name Episode 38 as their anime correspondent and en-WP's episode-list lead names 38 as the last manga-based episode. (2) On row 36 AFG makes NO filler claim: the cell maps '36, 37' positively and the blue class carries a faithfulness note about ch 37 p.18 onward. The stored/AFG 'canon/mixed' contradiction on 36 is therefore an artifact of typing AFG's CLASS rather than reading its NOTE — the wave-1 finding, reproduced. CHAPTER SPACE: one space throughout. Our stored total_chapters = 117 against latest_known = 113 is consistent with the bonus chapters being counted as UNITS by AniList and not as numbers by the books — the mainline ceiling is 113 and volume 9's printed contents are 32, Bonus, 33, 34, 35 (en-WP). SOURCES BEYOND AFL AND AFG: (1) souleater.fandom via the MediaWiki API — Episode 32, Episode 36, Episode 38, Chapter 32.5, Chapter 37, Chapter 38, Chapter 39, read in BOTH directions (episode -> chapter and chapter -> episode); note the wiki host is souleater.fandom, not soul-eater.fandom (404). (2) en-Wikipedia — List of Soul Eater chapters (volume 9's printed contents) and List of Soul Eater episodes (its lead's 'After episode 38, the anime deviated' plus per-episode summaries for 32, 36, 38). (3) ja-Wikipedia ソウルイーター — the 各話リスト and the prose. NOTE ON ja-WP AS A MARKER SOURCE for this series: its episode-list bolding is NOT an original-episode marker here — the legend reads '話数が太字の回は前述「ソウルイーター ベストセレクション」で再放映されたもの' (bold = re-aired in the Best Selection), so there is no per-row ja-WP claim to weigh; its only typing statement is the block prose '第36話までは原作の展開を踏襲していたが、原作への追いつきに伴い第37話以降はアニメオリジナルストーリーとして独自の物語で完結した', which is coarse and already superseded per-row by the stored rulings and by en-WP.
structure.coverage_set_checked: ep 31 -> END 32 {30-32}; ep 32 = the vol-9 bonus chapter only, no mainline pages, position-less; ep 33 -> 33; ep 34 -> 35 {34-35}; ep 35 -> 36 {35-36}; ep 36 -> END 37, START 36 {36-37, ch 37 through ~p.30}; ep 37 = filler (stored, ch-38 slivers only); ep 38 -> END 39, START 38 {38-39, partial}; ep 39+ = the studio ending. No mainline chapter is stranded by leaving ep 32 position-less, and the 36 -> 38 frontier is unchanged.

flags_for_sean: AFG's red '* Filler' + 'N/A' pair means TWO different things on this page and the difference matters to the T4 strong-tier flag: on ep 32 the 'N/A' is a true statement about the chapter NUMBER (the source is an unnumbered tankobon bonus chapter) while the red class is false, and on ep 17 the same pair is entirely correct (ep 17 'Legend of the Holy Sword 2' is anime-original and AFL agrees, so it never entered the flag). A red AFG row whose episode adapts an unnumbered bonus chapter is a recurring shape — this is the third instance in the catalog after bleach eps 46 and 227 — and it will keep generating strong-tier contradictions that resolve as 'canon, A44 position-less', not as retypes.

AFG's BLUE class is not a type on this page. Row 36's blue cell maps '36, 37' and its note is a faithfulness observation ('there are changes compared to the manga ... chapter 37 ... from page 18 onward'). If the T4 flag maps blue -> mixed it will keep manufacturing contradictions against correctly-typed canon rows; consider reading the note text for 'Filler' / 'Mixed' wording before classing a blue row.

OUT OF SCOPE but recorded: souleater.fandom's Episode 36 trivia says 'Black Star's fighting technique Shadow Star: Gathering Cutter was later added in the Manga during the manga's take on the fight on Lost Island'. That is an INCORPORATION-shaped claim, but it is a TECHNIQUE, not events, and the catalog's rule is explicit that designs without events are not an adoption basis — so I did NOT propose an adopted{author} annotation. If it ever matters, the events question would be whether Ohkubo wrote the anime's Lost Island outcome into the manga, and the answer from ch 37 is no (the manga's Mosquito escapes).
